messages:
Kevin: Heads-up — I see a perf regression tied to streamed responses + aggressive coalesce. p95 up ~60ms for short chats after the latest batcher change.

Maya: ugh. repro on staging or prod? :eyes:

Kevin: Staging first. Repro steps: send 1000 short-chat requests (~12 tokens each) at 200 rps with streaming enabled and coalesce window=8ms.

Kevin: Quick numbers:
```
Before: p50=18ms p95=42ms p99=120ms  GPU util=62%  avg batch=5
After:  p50=20ms p95=100ms p99=260ms GPU util=71%  avg batch=14
```

Priya: those avg batch sizes jump looks suspicious — streaming should not hold up tiny messages that long. Could be partial-decode scheduling delaying flushes while waiting for larger batches.

Sam: any kernel fallbacks in the trace? sometimes bigger batches trigger a different kernel path and KV warmup stalls.

Kevin: I profiled a few runs, attached snippet from the cpu->gpu handoff timeline:
```
[timeline]
0.0ms accept
1.2ms queue_wait
5.6ms coalesce_wait
8.1ms kernel_select -> small_kernel
8.3ms partial_decode wait (kv_lock)
11.7ms fallback -> medium_kernel
11.9ms gpu_dispatch
```

Kevin: Note the partial_decode wait on kv_lock right before kernel selection in many traces. When coalescing grows, we seem to contend in KV cache population and then select a fallback kernel which has worse latency for short streams.

runtime-bot: perf-alert: staging/streamed-coalesce experiment crossed p95 threshold at 2026-03-18T15:22Z. trace: https://perf.internal/runs/3401239876

Maya: hmm. options: tighten coalesce window for streaming, or make partial-decode preemptive (do partial decode asap and flush early), or make kernel selection prefer low-latency kernel for streams even if throughput suffers.

Priya: preemptive partial-decode seems promising. Also we should avoid kernel fallback churn — consider kernel pinning for requests with stream=true for the first N tokens. That avoids the warmup+fallback loop.

Sam: simpler quick test: drop token_budget_target from 64->32 and reduce coalesce window 8ms->4ms for stream routes. See if p95 improves. Maya can run A/B?

Maya: i'll run two variants on staging now:
```
A: coalesce_window=4ms token_budget_target=32 partial_decode=standard
B: coalesce_window=8ms token_budget_target=64 partial_decode=preemptive
```

Maya: starting run A now, will push ~200 rps for 10m and capture traces.

Kevin: FYI kernel selection tweak I'd like to try if A/B not good: prefer "small-latency-kernel" for any stream route when expected seq_len < 64. cheap guard.

Priya: watch for KV thrash — if we reduce batch sizes we reduce cache reuse and that can up GPU work per-token. We need to measure token cost too, not just latency.

Maya: Run A finished: p95 down to 48ms (from 100ms). avg batch=6. GPU util 66%. token cost +3%. traces: https://perf.internal/runs/3401239888

Sam: nice win on latency. +3% token cost is okay for streaming product routes.

Priya: good. Run B?

Maya: Run B (preemptive partial-decode) results: p95=46ms avg batch=7 GPU util 68% token cost +1.2%. traces: https://perf.internal/runs/3401239896

Kevin: both look promising. Preemptive partial-decode has slightly better p95 and less cost hit. Suggest we roll preemptive partial-decode for stream routes behind a feature flag and keep coalesce_window relaxed.

Sam: agree. Can someone make a short rollout plan + observability checks? we need p50/p95/p99, token cost, and KV hit rate.

Priya: I'll add an extra KV warmup metric and a kernel-switch counter to the dashboard. set alert if kernel_switch_rate > 0.5%/min.

Maya: I'll open the rollout PR and enable behind flag on staging + dedicated canary on prod. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge/1234

Kevin: thanks. follow-up tickets:
- tune token_budget_target per route (Sam)
- kernel-pin policy for stream route (Priya)
- rollout + dashboards (Maya)

Sam: assigning tickets and adding owners. tagging @oncall for a watch during prod canary. :thumbsup:

Kevin: sweet. FYI I'll dig into a few traces where kernel fallback still happens after preemptive decode — might be a race with KV population.

Maya: cool. keep updates here.

runtime-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for feature "preemptive-partial-decode-streams" at 2026-03-18T16:12Z

Sam: marking follow-ups in the sprint and closing this thread once rollout flag is stable.
